Chapter 9: Creating a Vision for the Future
Once you and your partner have developed new habits around communication, healing, and staying connected, there’s a natural next step—looking ahead, together.
Building a shared vision for your future isn’t about mapping out every detail. It’s more like creating a living, breathing document that captures both of your hopes, dreams, and values.
So, what does a shared vision actually include? Well, it could be anything from how you want to handle conflict and support each other’s growth, all the way to the kind of family or home you want to create.
Maybe you picture traveling together, learning new things, or getting involved in your community. Or perhaps you see yourselves embodying values like kindness, honesty, or even a sense of adventure.
Here’s a simple way to get started: set aside some time just to dream together. Ask each other questions like, “What do we want our life to look like in five years?” or “How do we want to feel in our relationship?”
Take turns sharing your ideas, no matter how big or small. The real magic happens when you blend your wishes into a vision that feels both inspiring and achievable for both of you.
You might notice this process feels energizing—especially if you’ve spent a lot of time lately focusing on problems. Instead of dwelling on what’s wrong, you’re shifting toward what’s possible, and seeing yourselves as true co-creators of your life together.
And here’s something really helpful: that shared vision becomes your touchstone during tough times. When challenges pop up—and let’s be honest, they always do—you can come back to your vision and ask, “Does this choice move us closer to the life we want?”
That simple question keeps you both grounded in purpose, and reminds you that your relationship isn’t just about overcoming obstacles—it’s about moving toward something meaningful, together.
